description.narrative: This project supported the transformation of urban development by demonstrating how transit-oriented urban development could reduce the growth in car traffic and simultaneously improve air quality. The government believed that a more holistic approach to transport planning and deployment was required, with better coordination of land-use and transport systems, and integration with social housing policy. Public and private investments (through Public Private Partnerships) were channeled into showcase projects across a range of locations and intervention types. The project promoted better-designed, walkable, transit-oriented neighbourhoods and contributed to reduced household transport costs, better access to jobs and services, and improved social inclusion in the respective area. This project reached 1,309 people through training and capacity development measures.
